title: Dispatch CSA 4: Two Survey Parties Report From the Same Plain
summary: The Institute’s instruments now register competing accounts of one expedition.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Messages received from the Calder aperture yesterday appear to place two versions of the survey party upon the same stretch of water. The first is the party that departed on Monday. The second, whose voices include the returned Professor Vey, has reported observations bearing dates six days ahead.

In the later account, the ranging anchor was set at a black stone marker to keep the aperture open. The water then began reflecting positions the party had not yet occupied. The returned Mr. Rook described these reflections as “routes awaiting a traveller.” He believes the anchor held several possible routes in place long enough for one party to reach Alderwick before it left.

The party presently in the Stratum has reached the marker but has not set the anchor. “There are our footprints,” Miss Quill said in a transmission played for the press. “They lead to the stone and stop. We have walked round it twice.” Her voice was steady until she described a fourth print appearing beside the others, made by a smaller boot like her own.

Dr. Marr cautions against calling either account a prediction. Records made on the far side have often proved difficult to place in sequence. Yet the Institute can test one detail: the returned party described a fracture in the black stone. A drawing transmitted by the departing Miss Bell this morning shows the same fracture.

Outside the Institute, Miss Quill’s father has asked the returned Professor Vey to explain what happened to his daughter. He has received no reply. The Miss Quill who crossed on Monday remains alive and has now heard the account of her own death.
